name: Pageable PLE / n-gram cache table
canonical_description: Keeps part of the prediction/lookup table pageable or outside resident memory to run an oversize build.
mechanism: Keeps the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next n-gram/PLE lookup table pageable or outside resident memory, typically through mmap, so a build whose total file set exceeds physical memory can run with the table fetched from host memory or disk.
constraints: The AtomicChat Flash-Next GGUF source records that mmap must stay on, --load-mode none must not be used, and -fit off is required for the recorded Metal lane.
A setup may record intentional pageability only when the source states it; silence about offload is not evidence of pageability or of no offload.
tradeoffs: The source may establish an intentional memory-shape mechanism without measuring cold-start behavior.
Expected cold-start behavior must remain a C1 mechanism claim or an open question; it may not be stored as an observed cold_start_effect.
re_review_triggers: llama.cpp or Metal changes PLE/mmap loading behavior.
The vendor card or build instructions change the PLE residency requirements.
A setup records a cold-start effect without a measured source.

canonical_sources.locator: 'Why this is possible', the AD-3.84bpw-IQ4_XS-M64 quant table, and the three run-requirement notes after the Metal command
canonical_sources.note: Vendor card recording the 51B n-gram lookup table, 45.8 GB in-memory plus 39.1 GB SSD/table totals, mmap pageability, and -fit off.

note: Canonical technique identity only. A setup-specific claim must still carry its own statement, source, locator, lineage, evidence level, and contrast kind.
